tob-10024: Thomas à Kempis’s devotional classic, better known as The Imitation of Christ, has guided Christians toward a simpler, humbler faith for six centuries. Written by a fifteenth-century German monk, it urges readers to turn inward, practice humility, and follow Christ’s example in daily life. This volume offers an alternative English translation of a book that ranks among the most printed works in Christian history.
tob-10824: The Path was the American Theosophical magazine, edited in New York by William Q. Judge. This volume gathers its first year’s issues — essays on karma and reincarnation, defenses of Theosophy, and practical guidance for seekers. It captures the movement’s early American voice, earnest and combative by turns.
tob-13324: These conversations with Brother Lawrence, a humble kitchen worker in a Paris monastery, contain some of the most loved spiritual advice ever written. He tells how he learned to turn even the clatter of pots into prayer, keeping his heart turned toward God through every task. Short and plain-spoken, the book speaks directly to ordinary working lives.
tob-4024: René Descartes wrote this short book to show how he built all knowing from the ground up — doubting everything until he hit bedrock: ‘I think, therefore I am.’ From that one stone he rebuilds God, the world, and the mind. The Discourse is the founding text of modern thought, set down with startling plainness.
tob-0144-54824: Cosmogenesis — the Secret Doctrine’s opening volume — unrolls Blavatsky’s vast tale of the All: rounds of making, root races, the whole occult time-chart. Built of Hindu world-ages and her own claimed seeings, it is the Everest of hidden-system building. Readers climb it or turn back.
tob-4224: Francis Barrett’s Magus — 1801 — woke English rite-wonder from sleep, boiling Agrippa and the wonder-books into a workman’s handbook. His Heavenly Intelligencer taught a generation of wonder-seekers. The book’s sway ran deep through the 1800s. It stays the landmark of Regency wonder-lore.
cia-0000109824: A September 1945 report on Shanghai's Japanese counter-espionage service and an agent handler called Hovans, with his network and activities. As the Pacific war ended, Allied intelligence was mapping the spy webs Japan had woven through China. The document is espionage archaeology — digging up a defeated enemy's secrets.
cia-0000119624: An estimated January 1968 document on upcoming American civil air negotiations with Czechoslovakia. Even enemies negotiated landing rights — aviation was too practical to leave to ideology. The entry shows diplomacy's unglamorous machinery turning beneath the grand Cold War narrative.
cia-0000124324: A March 1952 report on American prisoners of war in Chekiang province, China. The POW trail led to China's southeastern coast, far from any battlefield. The entry shows how widely the prisoners were dispersed — and how far the search had to reach.
cia-0000132624: A June 1960 report: Uruguay and Brazil considering expelling Cuban diplomats. The continent's giants were losing patience with Havana's provocations. The document is the expulsion, considered: the diplomats, nearly persona non grata.

arxiv-2605-08824: Realistic digital hair is notoriously hard — every head carries a hundred thousand strands. Haimin Luo, Min Ouyang, Lan Xu, and Jingyi Yu treat each strand as a sentence in a language, training an autoregressive model — HairGPT — to generate lifelike 3D hairstyles one strand at a time. The 2026 paper brings language-model machinery to computer graphics.
arxiv-2605-08924: Proteins do their work by touching each other, and describing those interactions in words would speed up biology. Xiao Fei, Sarah Almeida Carneiro, Yang Zhang, and colleagues present PPI2Text, which captions protein-protein interactions using coordinate-aligned pair-map decoding. The 2026 paper translates molecular handshakes into readable text.
arxiv-2605-09024: Virtual film sets built from Gaussian splats look great until the director changes the lighting. Adrian Azzarelli, Nantheera Anantrasirichai, James Pollock, and colleagues make the splats relightable, using image-based illumination to re-light captured scenes. The 2026 paper is virtual-production tech for flexible filmmaking.
arxiv-2605-09124: Finding bugs in smart contracts is not enough — what comes after detection? Tamer Abdelaziz looks beyond detection in smart contract security, toward response, repair, and resilience. The 2026 paper argues the young field must grow past its scanner phase into full incident response.
arxiv-2605-09624: Materials discovery is going AI-powered, and students need preparation aligned with real research workflows. Dongming Mei, Katherine Moore, and Ben Sayler propose a framework for building AI literacy in the field. The 2026 paper is education research for the autonomous lab era.
arxiv-2605-09724: Grokking — sudden generalization long after memorization — may come down to model capacity. Yiding Vincent Song and Hanming Ye argue capacity determines it through competing memorization and generalization speeds. The 2026 paper finally demystifies one of deep learning's strangest curiosities for good.
arxiv-2605-10024: Tidal disruption events — stars shredded by black holes — drive winds from hot accretion flows; hydrodynamical simulation captures the outflow. Mingjun Liu, De-Fu Bu, Xiao-Hong Yang, and colleagues run the simulations. The 2026 paper is black hole astrophysics with stellar debris.
plos-pone-0003424: Cell biologists watched receptor pairs change shape in this 2008 imaging study. Using fluorescence resonance energy transfer, which glows when molecules sit close together, they tracked the CXCR4 and CCR5 receptors, both doorway proteins HIV exploits. Binding of chemokine signals reshuffled the receptors' pairing, revealing how outside messages remodel the cell's surface machinery.
plos-pone-0003524: Parasitologists compared a thief's many disguises in this 2008 paper. Trypanosoma cruzi, the Chagas disease parasite, coats itself in sialic acid stolen by its trans-sialidase enzyme, and the gene comes in many flavors. Testing that diversity with catalytic antibodies, the team explored why the parasite keeps so many variants of its sugar-stealing tool.
plos-pone-0003624: Systems biologists Aon, Roussel, and Cortassa found cellular rhythms with no single tempo in this 2008 paper. Analyzing time series from the cell's energy machinery, they showed eukaryotic cells run on scale-free dynamics, with fluctuations at every timescale. The finding suggests the cell's clockwork is less metronome, more fractal.
plos-pone-0003724: In 2008, Yang, Harrington, and Vartanian found the secret to repeatable gene chips: shuffle the work. Randomizing the order of lab steps proved key to getting reproducible microarray results across runs. The simple fix targets a hidden source of the batch effects that plagued early gene-expression studies.
plos-pone-0003824: A 2008 plant genetics study watched parental genomes battle for the nucleolus. In hybrids, one parent's ribosomal DNA loci dominated through nucleolar dominance, with the winning NORs boosted by chromatin dynamics. The work reveals how cells pick a side when two genomes collide.
plos-pone-0003924: In 2008, Klemm, Eipel, and Cantre found a popular drug backfiring on the liver. Repeated doses of erythropoietin, meant to help, instead slowed liver regrowth in rats. The extra EPO raised TNF-alpha and tipped the Bax to Bcl-xL balance toward cell death. The cautionary result warns surgeons against overusing EPO around liver operations.
plos-pone-0004024: In 2008, Sakihama, Sato, and Iwanari unveiled a detector for shy protein handshakes. Their baculoviral display method catches the weak, low-affinity membrane protein interactions. Such fleeting contacts drive the cell recognition behind immune and neural systems. The simple detection tool finally opens weak protein interactions to systematic study.
plos-pone-0004124: In 2009, Mairal, Nieto, and Pinto armed drug design with iodine. Iodine atoms on drug scaffolds blocked transthyretin fiber formation. TTR misfolding drives about twenty amyloid diseases. The halogen trick guides stronger stabilizer drugs. The iodine anchor points the way to better anti-amyloid pills.
plos-pone-0004224: In 2009, Jackson, Higgins, and Lin tested fungal color mutants in wax moths. Conidiation color mutants of Aspergillus fumigatus proved highly pathogenic to the insect host. Spore color tracked with virulence in the moth. The cheap moth model speeds antifungal screening.
plos-pone-0004324: In 2009, a German team tested a stress-hormone forecast. A combined steroid/CRH test predicted drug response in sad inpatients. The hormone challenge flagged likely responders. The test could tailor depression care well. The 114-patient study backs clinical use of the test.
plos-pone-0358224: Bridges and buildings hum with vibrations — and damage changes the tune. This paper presents SpectralTCN, a neural network that reads vibration signals at multiple resolutions to detect structural damage. By catching the subtle frequency shifts of cracking or weakening, it offers an early-warning system for infrastructure.
plos-pone-0356524: How cancer patients see their illness shapes how they cope with it. This cross-sectional study at Bhaktapur Cancer Hospital linked illness perception to resilience among cancer patients. The connections point to which beliefs help patients bounce back — and which ones drag them down into despair.
plos-pone-0342524: Nurses who absorb others’ suffering can burn out with compassion fatigue — and prediction could prevent it. This paper published a protocol for a systematic review and critical appraisal of prediction models for compassion fatigue in nurses. The planned review will sort the models that work from the ones that don’t.
plos-pone-0341524: Nomophobia — the fear of being without one’s phone — grips students hard. This Bangladeshi study measured its prevalence and associated factors among medical and university students. The findings diagnose digital dependence in a population that can least afford the distraction.
plos-pone-0357124: In Nigeria, household wealth protects children against stunting — but not against wasting. This analysis of the 2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey found wealth associated with reduced stunting yet no link to wasting. The distinction refines nutrition policy: different malnutrition needs different fixes.
plos-pone-0356624: Infected joint replacements pose a brutal choice: rip out the implant or try to save it. This paper reported prosthetic joint infection eradication outcomes for the DAIR procedure — debridement, antibiotics, and implant retention — broken down by culture etiology. The bug-by-bug results tell surgeons when DAIR works and when it doesn’t.
plos-pone-0354924: Keratoconus — a progressive thinning and bulging of the cornea — blinds young people if caught too late. This paper combined machine learning with classic logistic regression to identify individuals at high risk and analyze the risk factors driving susceptibility. The dual approach gives eye doctors both predictive power and interpretable risk profiles, so screening can target the people most likely to develop this sight-threatening condition before vision is lost.
plos-pone-0354124: Neonatal E. coli infections kill newborns worldwide — and the bacterial O-serotypes behind them vary by region. This paper published a protocol for systematically analyzing global O-serotype prevalence of neonatal extraintestinal pathogenic E. coli, integrating previous research with bioinformatics. The planned synthesis will map which serotypes threaten newborns where — critical intelligence for vaccine design.
plos-pone-0342624: In England, struggling with English can mean struggling with health. This routine health records study explored health inequalities by language proficiency. The population-scale findings quantify a disparity hiding in plain sight — and demand that the NHS treat language access as the health intervention it is.
plos-pone-0355224: Who you know shapes how high you climb — even in government. This paper examined social networks as pathways of political mobility in Portuguese governments. The network analysis reveals how connections, not just competence, propel careers in Lisbon’s corridors of power — with lessons for democracies everywhere about merit versus mates.
plos-pone-0355724: Men and women drive differently — and road type matters. This developing-country case study examined differences in traffic safety behaviors between male and female drivers across road categories. The gendered patterns inform road safety campaigns that speak to how people actually behave behind the wheel.
plos-pone-0355124: Predicting which tuberculosis treatments will fail could save lives and stop resistance. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined AI and machine learning prediction of TB treatment failure. The synthesis separates the models that genuinely forecast failure from the ones that merely fit past data.
europmc-pmc2791224: The World Health Organization built a 12-question survey to measure disability, and this 2009 paper publishes the benchmark scores for it. Researchers tested the WHODAS 2.0 short form across populations so doctors and researchers can compare a patient's score against normal ranges. The data turned a useful questionnaire into a standardized measurement tool.
europmc-pmc2821324: Building gene sets for tree-of-life work means rounding up the right DNA reads, a dull chore. This 2010 paper brings BLAST-EXPLORER, a tool that builds such sets on its own. The authors show how it cuts the slog. The program took the tedium out of prepping tree studies.
europmc-pmc2832624: Care rules help no one if doctors ignore them. This 2010 review looks at how ideas from theory shape drives to spread care rules, and how tests of those drives get read. The authors find theory often missing or misused. Their critique pushed the field toward tidier thinking.
europmc-pmc2854724: Thousands of store chemicals await safety tests, and this 2010 paper fronts a fast screen. The authors unveil ToxCast, lab-dish tests that rank which chemicals merit deep probes. Their plan triages the flood. The scheme let rule-makers aim scarce test funds.
europmc-pmc2865524: When wild weeds bloom shapes their survival, and this 2010 paper hunts the genes. The authors map flowering time in Arabidopsis thaliana growing wild, using linkage and association methods. Their field-based hunt grounds lab genetics in nature. The work shows how wild plants tune their calendars.
europmc-pmc2868024: Getting antibodies into the brain is half the battle in Alzheimer's. This 2010 mouse study uses image-guided focused ultrasound to shuttle antibodies past the barrier, cutting amyloid-beta plaques. The authors show the combo works in a mouse model. The technique opened a new delivery route for brain drugs.
europmc-pmc2903524: Babies born with too little thyroid hormone need swift treatment to protect their brains. This 2010 review covers congenital hypothyroidism, how it is found, and how it is treated. The authors stress that newborn screening saves minds and futures. Their review backs one of public health's quiet triumphs.
europmc-pmc2922724: Heavy metal poisoning needs a way to pull metals out. This 2010 review covers chelation in metal intoxication. The authors survey the chelators, their uses, and their risks. Their overview guides emergency treatment of poisoned patients. Lead, mercury, and arsenic cases all draw on its guidance.
europmc-pmc2923524: Red pigments make apples blush, and this 2010 paper finds a gene switch behind them. The authors identify an R2R3 MYB factor that regulates the anthocyanin pathway in Rosaceae fruits. Their work explains how apples and kin paint themselves red. Breeders can now select for color with DNA markers.
europmc-pmc2928124: Cell skins differ by address, and this 2010 paper proves it. The authors compare the membrane-spanning parts of proteins across cell compartments. Their survey shows each compartment tunes its proteins its own way. The work helps biologists read membrane biology.
europmc-pmc3020924: Early HIV antibodies hint at vaccine paths. This 2011 paper studies the first broad antibodies people make against HIV. The authors reveal these early responders. Their work guides vaccine design. They appear within months of infection. Vaccines aim to summon them on demand.
europmc-pmc3022524: TB screening in HIV patients needed a standard rule. This 2011 paper builds a simple TB check for people with HIV in poor settings. The authors' rule saves lives. Their work shaped WHO guidance. Four questions and a scale do the job.
europmc-pmc3056724: B cell help needs two messenger proteins. This 2011 paper shows IL-21 and IL-6 steer B cell immunity and helper T cell growth. The authors reveal the teamwork. Their work guides vaccine design. The pair can cover for each other. Flu shots lean on this teamwork.
europmc-pmc3060824: Algal toxin moonlights as a stress shield. This 2011 paper shows the microcystin poison shields its maker from oxidant stress. The authors reveal the hidden role. Their work reframes the toxin. Blooms may brew it for self-defense. Water managers watch for the blooms.
europmc-pmc3072524: A Parkinson's skin patch eased mornings. This 2011 RECOVER trial tests a rotigotine patch for morning stiffness and poor sleep. The authors' blinded trial shows benefit. Their work shaped care. Patients woke moving instead of frozen. The patch won approval in many countries.
europmc-pmc3080924: Dirty air harms the vulnerable most. This 2011 review asks who suffers most from particle pollution. The authors survey the evidence. Their overview guides clean-air rules. Kids, elders, and the ill top the list. Genes and poverty amplify the harm.
europmc-pmc3098824: Long non-coding RNAs drive cancer. This 2011 review surveys the dark-matter RNAs active in human tumors. The authors map the key players. Their overview guides cancer doctors. HOTAIR became the most infamous example. Drugs that silence them are in testing.
europmc-pmc6515324: Skin is more than a wrapper - it houses a full immune outpost guarding against germs, wounds, and sun damage. This review maps the resident immune cells patrolling skin tissue and the chemical, physical, and microbial barriers they maintain. Understanding this local defense network matters for treating eczema, psoriasis, skin infections, and even how wounds heal.
europmc-pmc6664124: Chitosan - a biodegradable polymer from shellfish shells - makes a promising drug ferry. This review covers chitosan nanoparticles for targeted delivery: easy to make, gentle on the body, and able to release drugs where needed. The natural material earns its place in nanomedicine.
europmc-pmc6715724: Alzheimer's neurons drown in calcium - and faulty mitochondrial drains may be why. This study shows impaired calcium efflux from mitochondria accelerates disease in Alzheimer's models. The jammed cellular plumbing links energy failure to neuron loss, spotlighting the mitochondrial exit door as a drug target.
europmc-pmc6723624: Penicillin's descendants still anchor modern medicine - and bacteria keep picking the lock. This review covers beta-lactamases, the enzymes that disarm these antibiotics, and the inhibitors designed to stop them. The 21st-century arms race between drug and bug, explained.
europmc-pmc6734524: Liver cancer resists treatment partly by corrupting its immune neighborhood. This review travels from bench to bedside: the tumor immune microenvironment of hepatocellular carcinoma and the immunotherapies trying to fix it. Understanding the local politics of the tumor guides smarter clinical strategies.
gao-gaoreports-b-299624: Tennier Industries took its July 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest against bid law. Every protest, big or small, gets the full fair-play reading.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-424: Homeland Security's tech buying needed a rulebook in 2007 — GAO's report says the department had to write and live by real IT policies. The findings demand the missing manual be finished. The report's refrain: big systems need big discipline, or big waste follows.
gao-gaoreports-b-299424: Global Solutions Network took its April 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest against bid law. Global name, local rules: the bid law applies exactly the same to everyone.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-224: The Army's officer pipeline was springing leaks in 2007, and GAO's report says a strategic plan was needed for accession and retention. The findings demand the blueprint. The report warns that the lieutenants of tomorrow needed a reason to stay. The ranks had to be kept full.
openalex-w7204669824: Parents shape what their children eat, but many never learned to cook well themselves. This scoping review maps programs that teach parents cooking skills and nutrition knowledge, aiming to bring home cooking back. The authors survey what has been tried and what the studies show. A public-health look at the kitchen as the front line of childhood nutrition.
openalex-w7204665824: Teaching Spanish at a university built for Afro-Brazilian and Lusophone exchange brings unique chances and hurdles. This experience report from UNILAB's language center describes teaching Spanish there: what worked, what was hard, and what it taught the instructors. The authors write from direct classroom experience. A lively account of language teaching at the crossroads of cultures.
pmc-13439124: A 2026 microbiology paper mapping the genome-wide network of antibiotic susceptibility in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a dangerous hospital pathogen. Testing which genes make the bacterium vulnerable reveals the full landscape of potential drug targets. The network view goes beyond single-gene resistance studies.
pmc-13435824: A 2026 veterinary imaging paper on what determines grayscale pixel intensity in ram testicular ultrasound — specifically how region-of-interest placement and imaging plane affect readings across age groups. Standardizing the methodology matters for breeding soundness exams. The study reports the methodological determinants in detail.
pmc-13433324: In this 2026 forest genetics paper, researchers ran genome-wide association studies in two range-edge populations of European beech to find the genes behind adaptation to climate change. Trees at the edge of their range face the strongest selection. The identified factors could guide which seed sources to plant as the climate shifts.
pmc-13428224: This 2026 population-based study documented early cognitive and behavioral changes in primary lateral sclerosis, a motor neuron disease related to ALS. Thinking and behavior changes are underrecognized in PLS. The findings argue for broader assessment beyond the motor symptoms.
pmc-13407324: A 2026 scoping review on building trust in newly established physician-patient relationships. First impressions in medicine shape adherence and outcomes, yet the trust-building process is under-mapped. The review gathers what is known and where the gaps are.
pmc-13392224: This 2026 neuroscience paper presents a multiscale algorithm that maps causal relationships across space and time to reveal how transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation — zapping the ear's vagus branch through the skin — affects brain networks. Understanding the mechanism could turn a promising technique into a reliable therapy. The causal mapping method is the core advance.
pmc-13381724: This 2026 trial found electroacupuncture effective against sarcopenia — age-related muscle loss — in patients on maintenance hemodialysis. Dialysis patients lose muscle fast, and the study tested a low-cost intervention. The positive result offers a practical therapy for a vulnerable group.
pmc-13354824: This 2026 toxicology paper investigated how PFOS and PFOA — "forever chemicals" — affect interleukin-17 signaling and related pathways (the title is truncated in the record). Immune disruption is a suspected PFAS harm. The study adds mechanistic evidence to the regulatory debate.
pmc-13526524: In this 2026 C. elegans paper, worms avoided EGCG — the green tea compound — through the SRXA-7 G-protein coupled receptor. The receptor mediates the aversive response. The finding maps a chemosensory pathway.
pmc-13470524: In this 2026 microbial ecology paper, continuous evaporative salinization drove microbial community transition and carbon metabolism plasticity in hypersaline brines. Salt concentrates life's ingenuity. The study details the adaptation.
pmc-13468924: This 2026 critical narrative review examined artificial intelligence dependency in college students. The emerging behavioral pattern worries educators. The review takes stock of the evidence.
pmc-13452224: A 2026 materials paper on a kinetically controlled shock-wave route to turbostratic boron-carbon-nitride nanosheets. The violent synthesis makes orderly nanomaterials. The route is the innovation.
pmc-13530524: This 2026 conference poster tested the validity and responsiveness of a two-question universal pain and function score for sports surgeries. The ultra-brief measure worked. The poster validates the shortcut.
pmc-13597124: In this 2026 bioinformatics paper, hicream — a flexible framework — identified significantly different regions in Hi-C chromatin data. The 3D genome comparison tool is the deliverable. The framework is the advance.
pmc-13487324: A 2026 electrophysiology paper comparing acute efficacy of a focal dual-energy contact force-sensing catheter versus standard radiofrequency for persistent atrial fibrillation ablation. The new catheter was tested. The comparison is the evidence.
pmc-13483624: This 2026 paper described SALGINTR — development and early evaluation of a low-cost cloud-based digital participatory surveillance system for influenza-like illness among physicians (the title is truncated). The doctors reported symptoms digitally. The system is the innovation.
pmc-13465024: This 2026 AI paper introduced SpecAtt-Net — time-frequency image representations of slice-level radiomic features for explainable lung cancer classification via slice-wise attention (the title is truncated). The attention mechanism explained itself. The network is the advance.
pmc-13477024: A 2026 paper showing eVLP compound delivery broke the prime editing efficiency ceiling. The virus-like particles delivered better. The breakthrough advances gene editing.
pmc-13451524: This 2026 single-cell RNA sequencing paper revealed interferon-gamma-related genes' role in primary Sjögren's syndrome. The autoimmune disease's single-cell landscape was mapped. The revelation is the mechanism.
pmc-13422124: In this 2026 realist evaluation, a roadmap to support international medical graduates toward satisfying rural general practice careers was developed. The IMG retention roadmap was the output. The approach is the realist evaluation.
pmc-13291924: In this 2026 veterinary case report, haemophilia A was diagnosed in a female German Shepherd homozygous for the FVIII p.C567Y variant in exon 11 of the F8 gene. The rare female hemophiliac dog was genotyped. The case documents the genetics.
pmc-13431024: This 2026 paper explored the impact of event-related and personal vulnerability characteristics on mental health after pandemic-related trauma exposure. The trauma's mental health predictors were mapped. The exploring informs care.
pmc-13428024: This 2026 case report presented blue rubber bleb nevus syndrome as severe transfusion-dependent anemia in an elderly patient — an unusual cause of lower gastrointestinal bleeding (the title is truncated). The rare syndrome's GI face was documented. The case teaches the differential.
pmc-13612224: A 2026 detailed analysis of invasive mold infection in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia — from the AIEOP-BFM ALL2009 clinical trial. The fungal threat was quantified. The analysis informs prophylaxis.
pmc-13421524: This 2026 chemistry paper presented a tetranuclear nickel hydride cluster capable of reversible activation of aromatic and aliphatic C-H bonds. The cluster's bond-breaking was reversible. The cluster is the catalytic advance.
pmc-13436824: This 2026 malaria paper showed FIKK1, a FIKK kinase family member, phosphorylated VAR2CSA and regulated adhesion of Plasmodium falciparum-infected red blood cells to the placenta (the title is truncated). The kinase controlled the placental binding. The regulating is the pregnancy-malaria mechanism.
arxiv-2606-16024: In the study of the early universe, a 'bubble' can mean a patch where the rules of physics swiftly changed — here, one that broke a pattern called O(4). This physics paper works out how such a bubble forms and acts. It is deep theory, meant for those who study how the young cosmos changed states.
arxiv-2606-16324: Light combs — lasers spitting matched rainbow hues — meter stuff with hair-line care, and heat-hues sniff chems best. This paper prints a thumb-size, twist-tuned heat-hue comb on a chip via bent-light tricks. For chip-light crews shrinking lab gear. Small combs mean field kits, not bench beasts.
arxiv-2606-16824: Serving chatbots means caching huge 'KV caches' — memory of past conversation. CacheWise studies real workloads and optimizes KV cache management so servers handle more users efficiently. It is for systems engineers running LLM services. Smart caches, more chats per box.
